message.content: In Christian theology, Jesus Christ is regarded as the central and ultimate fulfillment of biblical prophecy. While the Old Testament contains many prophets—such as Isaiah, Jeremiah, and Daniel—who foretold events and themes that Christians believe point toward Jesus, the New Testament presents Jesus himself as the culmination of those prophetic expectations. Thus, within mainstream Christian belief, Jesus is seen as the most significant prophetic figure, though interpretations and emphases can vary among denominations and traditions.
